summary: Texas Forest Service steel tower at Ratcliff, Houston County, one of two 90-ft towers completed 1928; listed standing; now inside Ratcliff Lake Recreation Area.

facts.design: steel lookout tower, 90 feet, with ladders, landing platforms and a glass-enclosed cabin about 8.5 feet square (1928 reports)

access.note: Inside the Ratcliff Lake Recreation Area, a Forest Service campground in the Davy Crockett National Forest, per a commercial site and the Forest Service page. Whether the tower itself can be climbed is not documented in the sources read.

events.note: Texas Forest Service, in co-operation with Southern Pine Lumber Co. and Houston County Timber Co., completed two 90-ft steel towers; one at Ratcliff, one on Bird Mountain
CCC Camp F-4-T built at the site in 1933-34; Davy Crockett National Forest established in the area in 1935; camp closed 1941
Ratcliff Lake Recreation Area built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
National Geodetic Survey station description: standard steel tower, painted gray, about 100 feet high, about 0.3 mile north of Ratcliff

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The two 1928 reports give 90 feet, and the 1942 survey description says about 100 feet. We recorded 27.4 m (90 ft), the height of the finished tower in the 1928 reports; the survey figure is approximate.
The Alto Herald item places Ratcliff in western Houston County, while the Forest Worker item says eastern Houston County. This is not settled by the sources read, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Read: the Forest Lookouts page (1928 Alto Herald and Forest Worker items, 1942 NGS station description), the FFLA Texas list, the HMDB CCC marker, the Pine Cliff Resort page (commercial; used only for the State Highway 7 access, the tower's place in the recreation area and the 'last standing' phrase), the USFS Ratcliff Lake page and the Recreation.gov listing (no tower mention). Two searches and five reads used. Not found: staffing, notable fires, whether the tower may be climbed, current owner of the tower itself. The HMDB marker says CCC workers built fire towers without naming this one. Check the Bird Mountain tower (Anderson County, listed Tower Gone) for its own story. The brief's 27.4 m height is supported by the 1928 reports; the 1942 survey gives about 100 ft.
